name: Badge
description: A badge is a small, non-interactive label for a status (“Paid”, “New”) or a count (3 unread). It comes in five tones, solid or subtle, and as a dot.
whenToUse: To show the status of an item in a list or table.
To show a count on navigation or an icon, e.g. unread messages.

whenNotToUse.text: For keywords people can remove or filter by.
For a message that needs reading.

anatomy.name: Text or count
anatomy.description: Short status or a number (max+ above max).

values.value: gray | blue | sky | indigo | purple | pink | orange | teal
values.meaning: Category hues with no meaning of their own: departments, projects, file types. Same in every brand.
Small corners; reads as a label in dense tables.
Neutral surface with a border; only the dot or icon takes the color.
Tinted; for statuses in lists. Default.
Filled; for counts that must stand out.
Shows text or a count. Default.
A small dot, e.g. “new activity”; needs label.

behavior.text: count above max shows “99+”. Pass label (“128 unread messages”) so screen readers hear the full meaning.
A dot has no text, so label is required.

content: One or two words, in sentence case.
Use the same words for the same status everywhere.

guidelines.do: Pair color with a word: “Overdue” in danger.
guidelines.dont: Use a red badge with no text to mean overdue.
guidelines.why: Color alone isn’t seen by everyone (WCAG 1.4.1).

guidelines.do: Give counts and dots a label.
guidelines.dont: Leave “3” to be announced on its own.
guidelines.why: “3” means nothing out of context to a screen reader user.
Badges don’t look interactive; use a Tag, Button or Link.

aria.when: label replaces the shown text for screen readers.

wcag.how: Text passes 4.5:1 on every tone in every theme.
Dots and counts get a text label.

examples.title: Count
examples.code:
import { Badge } from '@ds/react';

<Badge appearance="solid" tone="danger" count={128} label="128 unread messages" />

examples.title: Dot
examples.code:
import { Badge } from '@ds/react';

<Badge dot tone="primary" label="New activity" />

examples.title: Category label
examples.description: A modern badge with a colored dot, e.g. a team in a table.
examples.code:
import { Badge } from '@ds/react';

<Badge tone="indigo" shape="modern" withDot>Design</Badge>

examples.title: Trend
examples.description: A change with an arrow icon.

examples.title: Announcement
examples.code:
import { BadgeGroup } from '@ds/react';

<BadgeGroup badge="New" href="/changelog">Dashboards are here</BadgeGroup>

changes: Eight category hues for tone; shape (pill, rounded, modern), size and bordered.
withDot, iconStart, iconEnd, image, onDismiss; icon-only badges.
New BadgeGroup: a badge with a message, optionally a link.

components.name: Badge
components.description:
A small label for a status, category or count, e.g. “Paid”, “Design” or 3 unread. Not
interactive, except for its optional remove button.

tone.description:
Color: a meaning (primary default, secondary, success, warning, danger) or a category hue
(gray, blue, sky, indigo, purple, pink, orange, teal).

appearance.description: `solid` for strong emphasis (counts), `subtle` (default) for status labels.

shape.description: `pill` (default) fully rounded, `rounded` small corners, `modern` neutral with a border.

bordered.description: Adds a thin border in the tone's color to subtle badges.

count.description: A number, e.g. unread messages. Shown as max+ above max.

dot.description: Shows only a small dot instead of text. Give it a label.

withDot.description: Adds a status dot before the text, e.g. ● Active.

iconStart.description: Decorative icon before the text. Alone (no text), the badge is icon-only: give it a label.

image.description: Small round picture before the text, e.g. a person or a country flag. Decorative.

onDismiss.description: Shows a remove button that calls this, e.g. for a filter.

dismissLabel.description: Accessible name of the remove button. Default "Remove {text}".

label.description:
Text for screen readers, e.g. "3 unread messages". Replaces what is shown; required for
dots, icon-only badges and bare counts, whose meaning isn't in the text.

components.name: BadgeGroup
components.description:
A badge with a message, e.g. “New · Dashboards are here →”, to announce something. With
`href` it is a link.

children.description: The message next to the badge, e.g. "We've just released a new feature".

tone.description: Color of the whole group. Default primary.

badgePosition.description: `leading` (default): badge first. `trailing`: message first, badge last.

icon.description: Icon after the message. Default an arrow when the group is a link; `null` hides it.
